items.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Honky Tonk, Bill Doggett. They were r-and-b guys who snuck into the pop charts, and I heard – that’s where I heard tenor.

ctx.x: Did you hear some of the r-and-b tenor players like Big Jay McNeely and Sam “the Man” Taylor?
Not at that time, no. These are solos from, like, Rock Around the Clock, that guy Rudy whatever his name was, a long Italian name. Duane Eddy had a great

saxophone player, Rebel Rouser. Then there were the little crossover things, as I know now, like Walkin’ with Mr. Lee, Lee Allen, Honky Tonk, Bill Doggett. They were r-and-b guys who snuck into the pop charts, and I heard – that’s where I heard tenor. Even In the Still of the Night has a great – no, Come Go with Me, my favorite song – the Del Vikings – my favorite song from that era has a great tenor saxophone solo with a giant squeak in the middle of it. I’m either thinking of Come Go with Me or In the Still of…
